column1: # Measured seconds per shell suite and node file, read by tests/lib/shard.py (its docstring holds the format and the
# rules): each entry's load in the full suite's shard split (ADR 0073 d3), so the shards balance on time, not file size,
# and node's order (shard.py --order: tests/run.sh starts node's files longest first, p54-3).
# tests/run.sh reads it too, for each shell suite's liveness bound (tests/lib/test-jobs.sh's suite_bounds): 10x the weight
# rounded up, at least 300 s, 1200 s for a suite with none (macOS CI runs a suite at up to 5.5x these local seconds). A
# suite whose seconds grow towards its bound needs this file regenerated, or it is killed as hung.
# Source: the per-suite `<label>: ok (<N>s)` lines of two local `make test` runs (2026-11-09, p43-6's audit,
# docs/audits/2026-11-09-test-suite.md), at the default cap of 4 on a 12-core Mac, load 3 to 5; each value is the
# median of the two. @merge-task-self-tests is its two self-tests summed. A suite that ended within its first
# second (0 s) is written as 0.5, since a weight must be positive.
# Node files (*.mjs, p54-3): the `<seconds><TAB><file>` lines of the `== node seconds per file` block that
# tests/lib/node-run.mjs prints at the end of node's phase (each file's top-level tests' duration_ms summed), from two
# local runs of every node file (2026-11-16, `bash tests/run.sh --only <them all>`, cap 4, the Mac under other rollouts'
# load), the median of the two; a file under 0.1 s is written as 0.1.
# Regenerate: run `make test` twice, take each suite's median from those lines and each node file's from that block,
# sum the two self-tests, and rewrite this file whole. A suite or node file added since falls back to its size times
# the median seconds per byte of its kind (shard.py).
# The four leg rows (tests/leg.test.sh and its parts leg-land, leg-rank, leg-security, split from it by p54-9) are
# leg.test.sh's 527 s split by the parts' measured shares of two local runs, until the next regenerate.
# tests/fast-tier.test.sh's row is its own, until the next regenerate: it grew from 24 s (2026-11-09) to 83 s, the
# median of two local runs (2026-11-18, `bash tests/fast-tier.test.sh` alone, a 12-core Mac at load 4 to 5), and
# 24 s gave it the 300 s floor, which master's macOS shard 3/4 passed at 259 s and then cut twice (run 44233636618).
